skills.name: Prepositions of time, place, purpose and direction

note.text: Prepositions express relations such as time, location or movement. In a simple school model, at can mark a clock time, on a day/date and in a longer period. In and on can locate something inside a space or on a surface; to can mark destination and into movement inside. For + noun can express purpose or intended use; to + base verb is an infinitive purpose construction, not the same grammatical pattern. Fixed combinations and context create exceptions, so do not apply a single word rule everywhere.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to choose a preposition or related purpose construction from the meaning of the whole phrase. Builds on: adverbials and clause relationships. Leads to: accurate descriptions, reports and movement narratives.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: The club meets on Monday in the afternoon. Bih waits at the entrance, walks into the room and puts a notebook on the table. A shelf is for books; members gather to read. The direction into differs from a position already in the room. Read the complete relation before choosing a small word.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Ask whether the phrase gives time, position, movement or purpose. Check what follows: for a noun, to a base verb in the purpose model. Do not confuse the prepositional use of to before a destination with every infinitive use of to.

key_words.meaning: a phrase locating an event in a temporal frame
a location without asserting movement into it
a relation showing movement towards or into a place
wording expressing intended use or aim

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: The notebook is on the table.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: On Monday gives the direction of movement. Correction: The named day locates time rather than destination.
On the table always means moving inside the table. Correction: It states where the notebook is in this model.
Into can only describe a stationary position with no movement. Correction: Into expresses the movement inside here.
For books and to read must have identical grammatical structure. Correction: A noun phrase after for differs from an infinitive after to.

e: Into suggests movement inside, not the stated surface position.
Towards gives direction.
